## Summary

This presentation reported the first ATLAS measurements of azimuthal flow in O+O and
Ne+Ne collisions at a nucleon-pair center-of-mass energy of 5.36 TeV. By comparing two
light nuclei of similar size but different predicted intrinsic shapes, the measurement
uses collective flow as a probe of nuclear geometry.

In the most central collisions, Ne+Ne exhibits approximately 10% larger elliptic flow
than O+O while the triangular flow of the two systems remains similar. Together with
multi-particle cumulant measurements, these observations provide evidence for the
elongated, bowling-pin-like geometry of the neon nucleus. The measured transverse-momentum
dependence of the flow harmonics also displays behavior qualitatively similar to that seen
in larger heavy-ion systems, supporting a collective origin for the observed anisotropy.
